svg.title: SHRED-MPC loop
svg.desc: Overlined vectors of sparse pressure observations and applied cylinder rotation history, each with L lag timesteps, enter a SHRED pressure surrogate containing the upstream SHRED-ROM architecture illustration. SHRED predicts pressure for candidate future rotations. The predicted mean pressure-lift output y_hat is compared with reference r using the tracking error e_k = y_hat_k - r_k. The optimizer minimizes J_k, the sum of tracking, oscillation and control-change costs. The selected first rotation segment advances the OpenFOAM CFD plant. New sparse measurements update the history and the process repeats.
svg.metadata:
Diagram formula sources are retained in each math SVG data-latex attribute. Tracking cost in the implementation is max(abs(e_k) - deadband, 0), with additional weighted lift-standard-deviation and normalized control-move penalties. Source: shred_mpc_launcher.py. Embedded image source: https://github.com/MatteoTomasetto/shred-rom/blob/main/media/SHRED-ROM.png MIT License

image.title: SHRED-ROM architecture, from Matteo Tomasetto's repository (MIT). Upstream reconstruction architecture used within this control-conditioned predictor.

svg.text: Advance the flow and return new sparse pressure data
At each MPC update: predict many candidate futures with SHRED, apply one control segment in CFD, then replan.
SHRED-ROM inset: Matteo Tomasetto – Stefano Riva (2024), MIT license. Architecture illustration; not a SHRED-MPC result.
